./docs/audits/codex-runs/2026-04-30-task-B2-pr-gate.txt:2764:docs/audits/codex-runs/2026-04-30-pre-task-0-followup-code-review.txt:613:   **Wave 1 evidence**: **instance #8** — ADR-0006 v1 commit codified reviewer-prompt mandates but did not update `agent-contract.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/pr-gate.md` / cross-link `team-operations.md` / regenerate `docs/review-checklist.md`; pr-gate caught the dogfood failure during R1 review of the close-ceremony bundle, forcing a v2 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form A — pre-regeneration omission)** — v5 bundle updated authority files (`agent-contract.md`, generator code, `team-operations.md` cross-link) but had not run the generator at all post-edit; the 3 regenerated outputs were stale at HEAD content; pr-gate caught this during R2 review, forcing a v6 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form B — staging-vs-working-tree confusion)** — v6 bundle ran the generator (so working tree had new content) but did NOT `git add` the regenerated outputs; the git **index** still held HEAD blob hashes for the 3 generated files; orchestrator confused `git status --short` "M" prefix (working-tree-vs-index) with index-vs-HEAD; pr-gate caught this via `git ls-files --stage` blob-hash comparison during R3 review, forcing the v7 fix that explicitly stages with `git add` + verifies via `git diff --cached`. **instance #12 (sub-form C — lockfile is a generated-from-authority artifact)** — Wave 1 close ceremony commit `e15ec36` ("fix(deps): commit pnpm-lock.yaml for @tailwindcss/typography (lockfile drift)"): the design-tokens erratum (commit `fdc86a8`) added the `@tailwindcss/typography` dependency to `package.json` but did not stage the regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`; CI install used the pre-update lockfile, drifted against the new `package.json`, and failed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Resolution: commit `e15ec36` staged the lockfile separately. Lesson codified: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump), `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the consumer-side generated artifact and must ride the same bundle — the class equivalence to `.claude/agents/*.md` regeneration is exact (deterministic derive + git-index staging required). The four sub-forms of the same item #8 class — pre-regeneration omission, post-regeneration commit-staging confusion, conceptually-correct-but-operationally-incomplete fix, AND lockfile-as-generated-artifact — together motivate the explicit operational sequence and `git diff --cached` canonical verification command codified above.

./docs/audits/codex-runs/2026-04-30-task-B2-pr-gate.txt:3064:docs/audits/codex-runs/2026-04-30-task-I1-code-review.txt:2331:   **Wave 1 evidence**: **instance #8** — ADR-0006 v1 commit codified reviewer-prompt mandates but did not update `agent-contract.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/pr-gate.md` / cross-link `team-operations.md` / regenerate `docs/review-checklist.md`; pr-gate caught the dogfood failure during R1 review of the close-ceremony bundle, forcing a v2 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form A — pre-regeneration omission)** — v5 bundle updated authority files (`agent-contract.md`, generator code, `team-operations.md` cross-link) but had not run the generator at all post-edit; the 3 regenerated outputs were stale at HEAD content; pr-gate caught this during R2 review, forcing a v6 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form B — staging-vs-working-tree confusion)** — v6 bundle ran the generator (so working tree had new content) but did NOT `git add` the regenerated outputs; the git **index** still held HEAD blob hashes for the 3 generated files; orchestrator confused `git status --short` "M" prefix (working-tree-vs-index) with index-vs-HEAD; pr-gate caught this via `git ls-files --stage` blob-hash comparison during R3 review, forcing the v7 fix that explicitly stages with `git add` + verifies via `git diff --cached`. **instance #12 (sub-form C — lockfile is a generated-from-authority artifact)** — Wave 1 close ceremony commit `e15ec36` ("fix(deps): commit pnpm-lock.yaml for @tailwindcss/typography (lockfile drift)"): the design-tokens erratum (commit `fdc86a8`) added the `@tailwindcss/typography` dependency to `package.json` but did not stage the regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`; CI install used the pre-update lockfile, drifted against the new `package.json`, and failed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Resolution: commit `e15ec36` staged the lockfile separately. Lesson codified: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump), `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the consumer-side generated artifact and must ride the same bundle — the class equivalence to `.claude/agents/*.md` regeneration is exact (deterministic derive + git-index staging required). The four sub-forms of the same item #8 class — pre-regeneration omission, post-regeneration commit-staging confusion, conceptually-correct-but-operationally-incomplete fix, AND lockfile-as-generated-artifact — together motivate the explicit operational sequence and `git diff --cached` canonical verification command codified above.

./docs/audits/codex-runs/2026-04-30-task-B2-pr-gate.txt:4019:    88	   **Wave 1 evidence**: **instance #8** — ADR-0006 v1 commit codified reviewer-prompt mandates but did not update `agent-contract.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/pr-gate.md` / cross-link `team-operations.md` / regenerate `docs/review-checklist.md`; pr-gate caught the dogfood failure during R1 review of the close-ceremony bundle, forcing a v2 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form A — pre-regeneration omission)** — v5 bundle updated authority files (`agent-contract.md`, generator code, `team-operations.md` cross-link) but had not run the generator at all post-edit; the 3 regenerated outputs were stale at HEAD content; pr-gate caught this during R2 review, forcing a v6 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form B — staging-vs-working-tree confusion)** — v6 bundle ran the generator (so working tree had new content) but did NOT `git add` the regenerated outputs; the git **index** still held HEAD blob hashes for the 3 generated files; orchestrator confused `git status --short` "M" prefix (working-tree-vs-index) with index-vs-HEAD; pr-gate caught this via `git ls-files --stage` blob-hash comparison during R3 review, forcing the v7 fix that explicitly stages with `git add` + verifies via `git diff --cached`. **instance #12 (sub-form C — lockfile is a generated-from-authority artifact)** — Wave 1 close ceremony commit `e15ec36` ("fix(deps): commit pnpm-lock.yaml for @tailwindcss/typography (lockfile drift)"): the design-tokens erratum (commit `fdc86a8`) added the `@tailwindcss/typography` dependency to `package.json` but did not stage the regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`; CI install used the pre-update lockfile, drifted against the new `package.json`, and failed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Resolution: commit `e15ec36` staged the lockfile separately. Lesson codified: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump), `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the consumer-side generated artifact and must ride the same bundle — the class equivalence to `.claude/agents/*.md` regeneration is exact (deterministic derive + git-index staging required). The four sub-forms of the same item #8 class — pre-regeneration omission, post-regeneration commit-staging confusion, conceptually-correct-but-operationally-incomplete fix, AND lockfile-as-generated-artifact — together motivate the explicit operational sequence and `git diff --cached` canonical verification command codified above.

# CLAUDE.md

> **GENERATED FROM agent-contract.md — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.**
>
> Edit `agent-contract.md` then run `pnpm generate:configs`. CI fails if drift detected.

This file is the Claude Code entry point for the **SelfKnowledgeBaseWeb** monorepo. It tells
every Claude session what the project is, the hard rules, the agent roster, and the workflow.

- Spec: [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-self-knowledge-base-design.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-self-knowledge-base-design.md)
- Active plan: [docs/plans/active.md](docs/plans/active.md)
- Single source for agents: [agent-contract.md](agent-contract.md)
- Codex tool invocations: [docs/runbooks/codex-tool-invocations.md](docs/runbooks/codex-tool-invocations.md)

## Hard rules

1. **File size**: 200 lines (target) / 300 lines (ESLint `max-lines` warn) / 500 lines
   (`pnpm size-check` hard fail). Spec §3.6.
2. **Cross-file references**: every doc/code change must keep doc cross-references and
   contract files in sync (`packages/*/CONTRACT.md`, `agent-contract.md`).
3. **Lychee link-check**: broken markdown links block merge. Run `pnpm link-check` locally.
4. **`pnpm check` is mandatory before requesting review** (lint + typecheck + test + build + size).
5. **No direct git from workers**: only `git-operator` may commit / branch / rebase / push.
6. **No web access from workers**: only `researcher` may `web_search` / `web_fetch`.
7. **No cross-package moves from workers**: only `refactorer` may reorganize packages,
   and every reorganization requires an ADR under `docs/decisions/`.

## Commands cheat-sheet

| Command                 | Purpose                                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm install`          | Install workspace dependencies                        |
| `pnpm dev`              | Run all `dev` scripts (parallel)                      |
| `pnpm check`            | Lint + typecheck + test + build + size-check          |
| `pnpm check:affected`   | Same, scoped to packages affected since `origin/main` |
| `pnpm size-check`       | Hard 500-line limit on every source file              |
| `pnpm link-check`       | Lychee scan over `./**/*.md`                          |
| `pnpm generate:configs` | Re-derive everything from `agent-contract.md`         |
| `pnpm format`           | Prettier write across the repo                        |

## Review workflow (spec §3.2 + ADR-0007 D2)

```
worker (writes code)
   │
   ▼
[Bash] codex exec --profile code-reviewer  (Codex 5.3-spark, line-level rigor, cheap default)
   │
   ├── if high-risk (D2 rows 1/2/4/8) → [Bash] codex exec --profile pr-gate  (Codex 5.5, deep scan)
   │
   ▼
pr-reviewer    (Claude, selective per ADR-0007 D2; spec match + regression + arch consistency)
   │
   ▼
git-operator   (Claude, only authorized git surface, runs `pnpm check` once more)
```

High-risk triggers per ADR-0007 D2 (4 rows +pr-gate +pr-reviewer, 4 rows +pr-reviewer only):
- **+pr-gate +pr-reviewer** (D2 rows 1/2/4/8): contract change, package add/remove, new ADR required, CI/deploy/auth/security touch.
- **+pr-reviewer only, skip pr-gate** (D2 rows 3/5/6/7): spec/agent-contract/ADR edit, delete/rename package, cross ≥3 packages, performance-auditor flagged.

See [ADR-0007 D2](docs/decisions/ADR-0007-job-function-codex-heavy-execution.md).

Codex tools (code-reviewer / pr-gate / plan-challenger / 5 scaffolders) are
[orchestrator-direct Bash invocations](docs/runbooks/codex-tool-invocations.md) post ADR-0007 D5,
not teammate spawns.

    97	function describePhase(phase: NnVizPhase): string {
    98	  switch (phase.type) {
    99	    case 'idle':

   114	function deriveLayerSpecs(
   115	  phase: NnVizPhase,
   116	  declarative: readonly LayerSpec[],
   117	): readonly LayerSpec[] {
   118	  if (phase.type === 'ready') {
   119	    const fromModel = layersFromModel(phase.model);
   120	    if (fromModel.length > 0) return fromModel;
   121	  }
   122	  return declarative;

   125	function layersFromModel(model: tf.LayersModel): LayerSpec[] {
   126	  const out: LayerSpec[] = [];
   127	  for (const layer of model.layers) {
   128	    const cfg = (layer.getConfig?.() ?? {}) as { units?: number; activation?: string };
   129	    const units = typeof cfg.units === 'number' ? cfg.units : 0;
   130	    if (units <= 0) continue;
   131	    out.push({ name: layer.name, units, activation: normalizeActivation(cfg.activation) });
   132	  }
   133	  return out;
   134	}

   136	const ACTIVATIONS: ReadonlySet<LayerSpec['activation']> = new Set([
   137	  'relu',
   138	  'softmax',
   139	  'sigmoid',
   140	  'tanh',
   141	  'linear',
   142	]);

   144	function normalizeActivation(raw: unknown): LayerSpec['activation'] {
   145	  if (typeof raw === 'string' && (ACTIVATIONS as Set<string>).has(raw)) {
   146	    return raw as LayerSpec['activation'];
   147	  }
   148	  return 'linear';
   149	}

     1	import type { LayerSpec } from '../core/serialize';
     2	
     3	/**
     4	 * Single authority for SVG topology layout across this package
     5	 * (ADR-0006 item #5 — algorithm + runtime constants replication).
     6	 *
     7	 * Both `NnViz.tsx` (React/NodeView path) and `NnViz.astro` (SSR path) MUST
     8	 * import `computeTopology` from here — never re-derive `SVG_WIDTH` /
     9	 * `SVG_HEIGHT` / `NEURON_RADIUS` / `MAX_VISIBLE_NEURONS` / column-step /
    10	 * row-step / edge enumeration / aria-label phrasing. ssr-render.test.ts
    11	 * exercises a corpus to detect drift if a future edit accidentally re-inlines
    12	 * the layout.
    13	 *
    14	 * Sister-pattern: `block-math/ui-default/render-math.ts` is the equivalent
    15	 * single-source authority for KaTeX rendering across Math.tsx + Math.astro.
    16	 *
    17	 * The function is pure (no React / DOM / tfjs imports) so it is unit-testable
    18	 * with vitest alone, and consumed identically from React renders + Astro SSR.
    19	 */
    20	
    21	export const SVG_WIDTH = 480;
    22	export const SVG_HEIGHT = 200;
    23	export const NEURON_RADIUS = 6;
    24	export const MAX_VISIBLE_NEURONS = 8;
    25	export const LABEL_BASELINE_OFFSET = 4;
    26	
    27	export interface TopologyNeuron {
    28	  readonly x: number;
    29	  readonly y: number;
    30	  readonly r: number;
    31	}
    32	
    33	export interface TopologyColumn {
    34	  readonly index: number;
    35	  readonly neurons: readonly TopologyNeuron[];
    36	  readonly label: string;
    37	  readonly labelX: number;
    38	  readonly labelY: number;
    39	}
    40	
    41	export interface TopologyEdge {
    42	  readonly key: string;
    43	  readonly x1: number;
    44	  readonly y1: number;
    45	  readonly x2: number;
    46	  readonly y2: number;
    47	}
    48	
    49	export interface TopologyDescriptor {
    50	  readonly width: number;
    51	  readonly height: number;
    52	  readonly columns: readonly TopologyColumn[];
    53	  readonly edges: readonly TopologyEdge[];
    54	  readonly ariaLabel: string;
    55	  readonly empty: boolean;
    56	}
    57	
    58	/**
    59	 * Empty / non-empty aria-label phrasing is part of the authoritative output —
    60	 * NnViz.tsx + NnViz.astro both consume `descriptor.ariaLabel` so neither path
    61	 * gets to inline its own copy. Pluralization rule: "1 layer" vs "N layers".
    62	 */
    63	function describeAriaLabel(layerCount: number): string {
    64	  if (layerCount === 0) return 'Empty neural network topology';
    65	  return `Neural network topology with ${String(layerCount)} layer${layerCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
    66	}
    67	
    68	export function computeTopology(layers: readonly LayerSpec[]): TopologyDescriptor {
    69	  const layerCount = layers.length;
    70	  const ariaLabel = describeAriaLabel(layerCount);
    71	  if (layerCount === 0) {
    72	    return {
    73	      width: SVG_WIDTH,
    74	      height: SVG_HEIGHT,
    75	      columns: [],
    76	      edges: [],
    77	      ariaLabel,
    78	      empty: true,
    79	    };
    80	  }
    81	  const colStep = SVG_WIDTH / (layerCount + 1);
    82	  const columns: TopologyColumn[] = layers.map((layer, i) => {
    83	    const x = colStep * (i + 1);
    84	    const visible = Math.min(layer.units, MAX_VISIBLE_NEURONS);
    85	    const rowStep = SVG_HEIGHT / (visible + 1);
    86	    const neurons: TopologyNeuron[] = Array.from({ length: visible }, (_, j) => ({
    87	      x,
    88	      y: rowStep * (j + 1),
    89	      r: NEURON_RADIUS,
    90	    }));
    91	    return {
    92	      index: i,
    93	      neurons,
    94	      label: `${layer.name} (${String(layer.units)}, ${layer.activation})`,
    95	      labelX: x,
    96	      labelY: SVG_HEIGHT - LABEL_BASELINE_OFFSET,
    97	    };
    98	  });
    99	  const edges: TopologyEdge[] = [];
   100	  for (let i = 0; i < columns.length - 1; i++) {
   101	    const left = columns[i]?.neurons ?? [];
   102	    const right = columns[i + 1]?.neurons ?? [];
   103	    for (let li = 0; li < left.length; li++) {
   104	      for (let ri = 0; ri < right.length; ri++) {
   105	        const a = left[li];
   106	        const b = right[ri];
   107	        if (a === undefined || b === undefined) continue;
   108	        edges.push({
   109	          key: `${String(i)}-${String(li)}-${String(ri)}`,
   110	          x1: a.x,
   111	          y1: a.y,
   112	          x2: b.x,
   113	          y2: b.y,
   114	        });
   115	      }
   116	    }
   117	  }
   118	  return {
   119	    width: SVG_WIDTH,
   120	    height: SVG_HEIGHT,
   121	    columns,
   122	    edges,
   123	    ariaLabel,
   124	    empty: false,
   125	  };
   126	}

     1	# ADR-0006: Cross-location asymmetry-audit checklist (process rule)
     2	
     3	| 字段 | 值                                    |
     4	| ---- | ------------------------------------- |
     5	| 状态 | accepted                              |
     6	| 日期 | 2026-04-30                            |
     7	| 作者 | orchestrator (Claude Opus 4.7 1M ctx) |
     8	| 触发 | Wave 1 codex 5.5 reviews caught 12 instances of the same meta-class across 6 tracks + 5 close-ceremony fix iterations (8 distinct items + 4 close-ceremony reinforcements of items #6 and #8) |
     9	| 替代 | 不替代任何 ADR；扩展 [ADR-0001](ADR-0001-stack-selection.md) §3.2 review chain |
    10	
    11	## Context
    12	
    13	Wave 1 implementation produced strong empirical evidence that **a single bug class** dominates the failure mode at line-level review:
    14	
    15	> **Cross-location asymmetry**: a value, schema, algorithm, or invariant exists in two or more places, and an edit to one location is not symmetrically applied to all peers, so behavior diverges silently.
    16	
    17	Across 6 tracks + 5 close-ceremony fix iterations, codex 5.5 (`pr-gate`) caught **12 instances** of this meta-class (8 distinct failure-mode items + 4 close-ceremony reinforcements of items #6 and #8). Every PR that lasted ≥ 2 review rounds hit at least one instance. The pattern is so consistent that linear "fix the cited blocker, ship v_n+1" iteration would not have caught the second-order asymmetry; codex specifically catches the symmetric counterpart that the worker missed.
    18	
    19	### Wave 1 empirical record (12 instances)
    20	
    21	| # | Track | Round | Asymmetry pair | Bug behavior |
    22	|---|---|---|---|---|
    23	| 1 | Track B (block-foundation + content-types) | R1 → fixed v3 | `listUIs` mutability vs `listCores` defensive copy | Caller mutation of return value polluted registry singleton |
    24	| 2 | Track D (apps/api) | R2 → fixed v4 | RFC 7235 `WWW-Authenticate` on framework-raised 401 vs custom `SkbError` 401 | 4 of 5 401 paths emitted spec-mandated header; the custom-error path silently dropped it |
    25	| 3 | Track F (editor-commands) | R3 → fixed v4 | `.strict()` on top-level Zod object vs nested `frontmatterSchema` | Top-level rejected unknown keys; nested still silently stripped them |
    26	| 4 | Track C (mdx-bridge) | R2 → fixed v4 | `marksEqual` link comparator: `href` only vs `href + title` | Same href, different titles silently merged into one link with the first title preserved |
    27	| 5 | Track F v5 | R3 → fixed v6 | One CONTRACT.md updated to reflect code; sister CONTRACT.md (`agent-tools`) had stale wording | Documentation-vs-code drift in the file the worker did not edit |
    28	| 6 | Track A | R1 → fixed v2 | FOUC inline IIFE saved-value algorithm + content schema | Truthy-coerce diverges from strict-whitelist for invalid / case-mismatched values; inline `z.object` redefinition diverges from `frontmatterSchema` authority |

    34	| 12 | Wave 1 close bundle v5 | R2 (pr-gate) → fixed v6 | Regenerated `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` + `.claude/agents/pr-gate.md` + `docs/review-checklist.md` were not staged in the bundle commit — authority + generator code updated, but generator outputs remained at pre-update HEAD content | Sub-form of item #8: regenerating an artifact and `git add`'ing it are separate steps; a bundle that updates authority + generator without staging the regenerated outputs is silently stale. Motivated the "verify by clean second-run" step now part of item #8. |
    35	
    36	Codex's structured review consistently caught these with three patterns:
    37	
    38	1. After fixing one location, **codex audits all peer locations** (not just the cited site)
    39	2. After a value/schema acquires an attribute, **codex audits every comparator/serialization function** for that attribute
    40	3. After a "happy path" fix, **codex audits the exception path** for the same equivalence
    41	
    42	These three habits collectively define the process rule below.
    43	
    44	## Decision
    45	
    46	Adopt an **8-point asymmetry-audit checklist** as a mandatory part of `code-reviewer` (Codex 5.3-spark, default cheap) and `pr-gate` (Codex 5.5, deep) review prompts. Reviewers MUST work through every applicable item before declaring PASS.
    47	
    48	### The 8 items
    49	
    50	1. **Field/attribute audit**: After adding a field to a data shape (Zod schema, Pydantic model, TS interface, mdast attrs, etc.), audit every comparator / equality / serialization / canonicalization function that handles this shape. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #4 — `marksEqual` link branch missed `title` when serialize emitted it.)
    51	
    52	2. **Status code audit**: After adding a status code to one HTTP handler (or, generally, an exit/error code to one branch), audit every other handler emitting the same code. RFC-mandated headers (RFC 7235 `WWW-Authenticate` on 401, RFC 7231 `Allow` on 405) attach to **the status code itself**, not the framework code path that emitted it. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #2 — custom `SkbError` 401 path missed `WWW-Authenticate`.)
    53	
    54	3. **Strictness audit**: After adding `.strict()` (Zod) / `extra='forbid'` (Pydantic) at one level of an object schema, audit every nested object/sub-schema. The strictness setting **does not propagate**; nested objects must opt in independently. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #3 — top-level `.strict()` shipped while nested `frontmatterSchema` still silently stripped unknown keys.)
    55	
    56	4. **Consumer schema audit**: After defining a schema in a single-authority package (e.g. `@skb/content-types/frontmatterSchema`), audit every consumer for inline duplicates or inline redefinitions that should `import` instead. The "deferred swap" pattern — "I'll inline now and import later" — is a contract break that compounds over time. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #6 part 2 — apps/site/content.config.ts inlined `z.object(...)` rather than importing `frontmatterSchema`.)
    57	
    58	5. **Algorithm + runtime constant replication audit**: When an algorithm or runtime constant is replicated outside its authority (e.g. inline FOUC scripts, login challenge derivation, pre-hydration boot logic that cannot import from packages), audit every consumer-side replica for byte-equivalent reproduction. The replica must register a **regression test** that asserts equivalence against the authority across a representative input corpus. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #6 part 1 — FOUC IIFE truthy-coerce vs `getInitialTheme()` strict-whitelist; remediated with `apps/site/src/__tests__/fouc-script.test.ts` 16-row corpus.)
    59	
    60	6. **Sister-file documentation audit**: After updating one CONTRACT.md (or any document that describes a code surface), audit ALL related CONTRACT.md files in the package family for sister-file drift. Two CONTRACT.md files that describe two halves of the same contract must use **identical terminology** for the shared identifiers (function names, schema names, refine predicate names). (Wave 1 evidence: instance #5 — `editor-commands/CONTRACT.md` updated to cite `editBlockInputSchema` while `agent-tools/CONTRACT.md` still referred to the old shape.)
    61	
    62	7. **Exception-scope equivalence audit**: When replicating an algorithm + its exception handling across files, audit BOTH the happy-path semantics AND the `try/catch` scope between authority and replica. Narrow vs wide `try/catch` can produce divergent fall-through behavior even with identical happy-path logic. Specifically: when `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / `IndexedDB` / `matchMedia` / any browser API in the algorithm path can throw, the `try/catch` MUST wrap ONLY the throwing call, with the fall-through branch (matchMedia / system default / DOM apply) running AFTER the catch handler — not inside it. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #7 — FOUC IIFE wide-scope try/catch swallowed matchMedia exceptions; remediated with narrow try/catch + 2 storage-throws regression tests.)
    63	
    64	8. **Authority-document → generated/consumed surface audit**: When updating an authority document (ADR, spec, `agent-contract.md`, runbook, CONVENTIONS) **OR a dependency authority (`package.json`)** that mandates behavior in downstream consumers, audit every consumer-side replica/generated artifact for synchronized update **AND staged-in-the-git-index in the same bundle**. Specifically: an ADR section that says "X file MUST be updated to do Y" requires the same commit to update X and provide a way to verify the synchronization. Generated artifacts (e.g. `docs/review-checklist.md` and `.claude/agents/*.md` derived from `agent-contract.md`; **`pnpm-lock.yaml` derived from `package.json`** — see sub-form C below) MUST be regenerated via the documented codegen step (`pnpm generate:configs` / `pnpm install`) AND **explicitly `git add`'d** so the git **index** (not just the working tree) contains the new content; runbooks (`docs/runbooks/team-operations.md`) MUST be cross-linked; Codex/Claude subagent prompt files MUST embed or reference the new rule.
    65	
    66	   **Operational sequence** (do not skip steps):
    67	   ```bash
    68	   # 1. Edit authority + generator code
    69	   # 2. Run codegen
    70	   pnpm generate:configs
    71	   # 3. Stage regenerated outputs (CRITICAL — see Pitfall below)
    72	   git add <regenerated/path/foo.md> <regenerated/path/bar.md>
    73	   # 4. Verify index reflects content (NOT just working tree):
    74	   git diff --cached --stat -- <regenerated paths>
    75	   #    → expects non-empty diff with the expected line counts
    76	   # 5. Verify idempotence: re-run codegen + confirm working tree matches index:
    77	   pnpm generate:configs
    78	   git status --short -- <regenerated paths>
    79	   #    → expects column-1 'M' (staged) + column-2 blank (working tree clean)
    80	   ```
    81	
    82	   **Pitfall (this is the load-bearing step)**: `git status --short` shows two columns: column 1 is index-vs-HEAD; column 2 is working-tree-vs-index. After running the generator without `git add`, you see `' M'` (space + M) — **working tree differs from index, but index still matches HEAD**. `git commit` only commits the index. Skipping `git add` means the regenerated content is in your working tree but NOT in the next commit. The bundle would land authority + generator-code changes WITHOUT the regenerated outputs, leaving consumers (Wave 2 reviewers reading `.claude/agents/*.md`) at pre-update content. Use `git diff --cached` (not `git status`) as the canonical staging-verification command — `--cached` shows index-vs-HEAD only, which is what `git commit` will produce.
    83	
    84	   **Pitfall extension — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is a generated artifact too (sub-form C below)**: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump / `@types/*` shift), `pnpm install` regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` as a deterministic derived artifact. Skipping `git add pnpm-lock.yaml` produces the same class of failure as skipping `git add .claude/agents/*.md`: working tree has the synced lockfile but the **index** still holds HEAD's stale lockfile, so the bundle ships `package.json` ahead of its lockfile. CI runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from the bundled state, sees the stale lockfile disagreeing with the new `package.json`, and fails install. The same `git diff --cached --stat -- pnpm-lock.yaml` canonical verification applies. (Wave 1 erratum commit `e15ec36`; codified as sub-form C below.)
    85	
    86	   Generated-from-authority files carry their own header comment ("GENERATED FROM agent-contract.md — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND") OR YAML frontmatter declaring authority source — both forms are acceptable. `pnpm-lock.yaml` lacks an explicit header (the format is fixed by pnpm) but is implicitly declared by `pnpm install`'s contract — its authority is `package.json` + the workspace `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
    87	
    88	   **Wave 1 evidence**: **instance #8** — ADR-0006 v1 commit codified reviewer-prompt mandates but did not update `agent-contract.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/pr-gate.md` / cross-link `team-operations.md` / regenerate `docs/review-checklist.md`; pr-gate caught the dogfood failure during R1 review of the close-ceremony bundle, forcing a v2 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form A — pre-regeneration omission)** — v5 bundle updated authority files (`agent-contract.md`, generator code, `team-operations.md` cross-link) but had not run the generator at all post-edit; the 3 regenerated outputs were stale at HEAD content; pr-gate caught this during R2 review, forcing a v6 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form B — staging-vs-working-tree confusion)** — v6 bundle ran the generator (so working tree had new content) but did NOT `git add` the regenerated outputs; the git **index** still held HEAD blob hashes for the 3 generated files; orchestrator confused `git status --short` "M" prefix (working-tree-vs-index) with index-vs-HEAD; pr-gate caught this via `git ls-files --stage` blob-hash comparison during R3 review, forcing the v7 fix that explicitly stages with `git add` + verifies via `git diff --cached`. **instance #12 (sub-form C — lockfile is a generated-from-authority artifact)** — Wave 1 close ceremony commit `e15ec36` ("fix(deps): commit pnpm-lock.yaml for @tailwindcss/typography (lockfile drift)"): the design-tokens erratum (commit `fdc86a8`) added the `@tailwindcss/typography` dependency to `package.json` but did not stage the regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`; CI install used the pre-update lockfile, drifted against the new `package.json`, and failed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Resolution: commit `e15ec36` staged the lockfile separately. Lesson codified: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump), `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the consumer-side generated artifact and must ride the same bundle — the class equivalence to `.claude/agents/*.md` regeneration is exact (deterministic derive + git-index staging required). The four sub-forms of the same item #8 class — pre-regeneration omission, post-regeneration commit-staging confusion, conceptually-correct-but-operationally-incomplete fix, AND lockfile-as-generated-artifact — together motivate the explicit operational sequence and `git diff --cached` canonical verification command codified above.
    89	
    90	### Wave 2 prep notes (forward-compatibility application)
    91	
    92	The 8 items have specific Wave 2 trip-hazards already identified by Wave 1's review record:
    93	
    94	- **Item #1 + Wave 2 attr-bearing marks**: when the first attr-bearing mark beyond `link` is added to mdx-bridge (e.g. `highlight: {color}`, `kbd: {style}`), the worker MUST simultaneously update `wrapMark` AND `marksEqual` AND add a fixture exercising attr-equality + attr-distinction. Default `return true` in `marksEqual` is a silent-drop trap for any attr-bearing mark. (See pr-gate Track C v4 R3 caveat.)
    95	
    96	- **Item #2 + Wave 2 new error categories**: when Wave 2+ adds new HTTP error categories (e.g. `auth-rate-limit`, `kernel-timeout`), each new `SkbError` subclass MUST emit the same RFC-mandated headers as framework-raised peers. Add a unit test asserting header presence per error type. (See `apps/api/CONVENTIONS.md` §5 Pitfall + Pitfall continued.)
    97	
    98	- **Item #5 + Wave 2 client-side replications**: when apps/site adds new client-side algorithm replications (theme variants beyond light/dark, locale negotiation pre-hydration, etc.), the worker MUST audit both saved-value semantics AND try/catch scope against authority. (See `packages/design-tokens/CONTRACT.md` Inverse-direction obligation invariant.)
    99	
   100	- **Item #7 + future inline scripts**: ANY future `<script is:inline>` block in the project that needs pre-hydration replication of a package algorithm MUST follow the FOUC template (narrow try/catch + corpus regression test).
   101	
   102	## Consequences
   103	
   104	### Positive
   105	
   106	- **Catch the failure mode proactively**: Wave 1 evidence shows reviewer-applied checklist would have caught all 12 instances on the first review round (including the close-ceremony dogfood instance #8 + the 4 fix-loop reinforcements), eliminating 12 round-trip cycles
   107	- **Reviewer prompt clarity**: code-reviewer + pr-gate codex profile prompts gain a concrete, enumerable checklist rather than the implicit "look for symmetric counterparts" expectation
   108	- **Worker self-audit**: workers gain a pre-PR checklist they can run before reporting `ready-for-review`, catching their own asymmetries (memory: `feedback_verification_fresh_state.md` showed the verification-rigor lesson; this checklist is the analogous rigor at code-design level)
   109	- **Empirical grounding**: 12 distinct instances spread across 6 tracks + 5 close-ceremony fix iterations make this rule data-driven, not a "best practice" speculation; instances #9-12 reinforce items #6 + #8 specifically through close-ceremony fix-loop evidence
   110	
   111	### Costs
   112	
   113	- **Review-round time**: applying 8-point audit at every review adds ~5-10 minutes per round of code-reviewer + pr-gate runtime. Acceptable trade-off given Wave 1 round-counts (Track F: 5 rounds; Track A: 3 rounds; Track C: 4 rounds; Track D: 4 rounds) — front-loading review thoroughness reduces total cycles
   114	- **Worker prompt overhead**: each spawn prompt now needs a reference to this ADR + the 8-point checklist. Marginal cost.
   115	- **False-positive risk**: items that don't apply (e.g. #2 "status code" doesn't apply to TS-only packages) need to be triaged and skipped. Reviewer profile prompts must explicitly say "skip items not applicable to this PR's scope" to avoid bloat.
   116	
   117	### Risks (mitigated)
   118	
   119	- **Risk**: workers might mechanically check items without thinking, producing false confidence. **Mitigation**: each item enumerates concrete failure modes from Wave 1, not abstract heuristics — easier to apply
   120	- **Risk**: this list might grow unbounded as Wave 2+ surfaces new asymmetry classes. **Mitigation**: ADR amendments are cheap; each new instance produces an ADR-0006 erratum capturing item #N+1. Wave 2 close ceremony reviews instances and adds items as needed.
   121	
   122	## Implementation
   123	
   124	### Reviewer prompt updates
   125	
   126	`code-reviewer` and `pr-gate` profile prompts MUST be updated to:
   127	
   128	1. State the 8-point checklist verbatim (or by reference to this ADR)
   129	2. Require the reviewer's verdict structure to include "asymmetry-audit applied: items {1..8} verdicts: ..."
   130	3. Explicitly mark FAIL if any applicable item is left un-audited
   131	
   132	`docs/runbooks/team-operations.md` §"角色与触发器" Tier 2 reviewer rows should cross-link to this ADR.
   133	
   134	### Worker pre-flight (template addition)
   135	
   136	Worker `ready-for-review` reports SHOULD include a brief asymmetry-audit summary: which of the 8 items applied, and the worker's self-audit verdict. Reviewers cross-check.
   137	
   138	### Wave 1 retroactive
   139	
   140	This ADR is **forward-applicable**. Wave 1 PRs that already shipped under earlier review without this checklist remain valid; the empirical instances they revealed are exactly what grounded this ADR. No retroactive re-review required.

    99	describe('computeTopology (SVG layout authority)', () => {
   100	  it.each(CORPUS)(
   101	    'corpus: $name → stable descriptor shape across React + Astro render paths',
   102	    ({
   103	      layers,
   104	      expectedColumns,
   105	      expectedNeurons,
   106	      expectedEdgeCount,
   107	      expectedAriaLabel,
   108	      expectedEmpty,
   109	    }) => {
   110	      const descriptor = computeTopology(layers);
   111	      expect(descriptor.width).toBe(SVG_WIDTH);
   112	      expect(descriptor.height).toBe(SVG_HEIGHT);
   113	      expect(descriptor.empty).toBe(expectedEmpty);
   114	      expect(descriptor.columns).toHaveLength(expectedColumns);
   115	      expect(descriptor.columns.map((c) => c.neurons.length)).toEqual(expectedNeurons);
   116	      expect(descriptor.edges).toHaveLength(expectedEdgeCount);
   117	      expect(descriptor.ariaLabel).toBe(expectedAriaLabel);
   118	      // Every neuron carries the canonical NEURON_RADIUS — locks the constant.

   130	      { name: 'b', units: 3, activation: 'relu' },
   131	    ]);
   132	    const keys = descriptor.edges.map((e) => e.key);
   133	    expect(new Set(keys).size).toBe(keys.length);
   134	    // 0-li-ri encoding: prefix is the source-column index.
   135	    for (const e of descriptor.edges) {
   136	      expect(e.key).toMatch(/^0-\d+-\d+$/);
   137	    }
   138	  });

   141	    const descriptor = computeTopology([

   143	    ]);
   144	    expect(descriptor.columns[0]?.label).toBe('dense_1 (4, softmax)');
   145	  });

   147	  it('called twice with structurally equal input returns structurally equal output', () => {

   149	    const b = computeTopology([{ name: 'l', units: 3, activation: 'relu' }]);

The topology authority itself is pure and both renderers import it. One risk has surfaced in the new `ssr-render.test.ts`: despite the filename/commentary, it currently tests only the `computeTopology` descriptor, not byte equality between React output and Astro SSR output; I’m checking whether another test covers that before calling it a finding.

     4	/**
     5	 * propsSchema for nn-viz block.
     6	 *
     7	 * `.strict()` is applied on BOTH the outer object AND the inner layer object.
     8	 * Reason: ADR-0006 #3 — Zod's `.strict()` does NOT propagate through nested
     9	 * z.object schemas. A user supplying `{layers:[{name,units,activation,bogus:1}]}`
    10	 * would slip past an outer-only `.strict()` because the layer item validator
    11	 * is a separate z.object that defaults to `passthrough`. We freeze the inner
    12	 * shape too so unknown keys at any depth fail loudly.

     1	# @skb/block-nn-viz Contract
     2	
     3	TensorFlow.js-backed neural-network topology visualization (Wave 2 Track E2).
     4	第二个 `viz-block-eng` 包；hand-craft（不走 codex-block-generator）。
     5	Sister-pattern E1 [@skb/block-jupyter](../block-jupyter/CONTRACT.md) 提供
     6	viz-block consumer 模式（lifecycle + abort + error triage），E3 (block-agent-flow)
     7	将继承同一框架。
     8	
     9	## Public surface
    10	
    11	五个 entry：
    12	
    13	- `.` (root barrel) — re-export `./core`
    14	- `./core` — headless 层
    15	  - `nnVizCore: BlockCoreDefinition<typeof propsSchema>` — name=`'nn-viz'` /
    16	    kind=`'viz'`（[ADR-0009](../../docs/decisions/ADR-0009-block-kind-union-expansion.md)）/ mdxComponent=`'NnViz'`
    17	  - `serializeNnViz(node) → mdxJsxFlowElement` — Tiptap → mdast (Wave 3 mdx-bridge routing 时启用)
    18	  - `parseNnViz(mdast) → TiptapNode` — mdast → Tiptap (同上)
    19	  - 类型: `NnVizTiptapNode` / `NnVizMdastJsxElement` / `LayerSpec`
    20	- `./ui-default` — presentational 层
    21	  - `nnVizUiDefault: BlockUIDefinition<typeof nnVizCore.propsSchema>` — uiId=`'default'`
    22	  - `NnVizEditorView` / `NnVizRenderView` / `NnVizView` — `ComponentType<NnVizViewProps>`
    23	  - `createTfjsBridge(opts) → TfjsBridge` — `@tensorflow/tfjs` consumer
    24	    pattern entry（per-block isolated `tf.LayersModel` + AbortSignal cleanup）
    25	  - 类型：`TfjsBridge` / `TfjsBridgeOptions` / `NnVizPhase` / `LoadLayersModelFn`
    26	  - `NN_VIZ_TOKENS: NnVizTokens` — design-token name witnesses
    27	- `./ui-default/NnViz.astro` — apps/site SSR consumer 直接 import 的 Astro 组件
    28	  （静态拓扑 SVG 占位：仅渲染声明式 `layers`，model 在客户端 hydration 后加载）
    29	- `./ui-default/nn-viz.css` — 视觉规则单一来源（design-token-bound，error/fg/muted/accent
    30	  color 走 `var(--color-*)`）
    31	
    32	### Consumer 使用方式
    33	
    34	`apps/site` / `editor-shell` 必须 `import '@skb/block-nn-viz/ui-default/nn-viz.css';`
    35	方能渲染 status / topology svg / slider controls。Astro page 直接
    36	`import NnViz from '@skb/block-nn-viz/ui-default/NnViz.astro';`。
    37	
    38	`propsSchema` 形状（见 `src/core/core-definition.ts`）：
    39	
    40	```typescript
    41	const layerSchema = z.object({
    42	  name: z.string(),
    43	  units: z.number().int().positive(),
    44	  activation: z.enum(['relu', 'softmax', 'sigmoid', 'tanh', 'linear']),
    45	}).strict();    // ⚠ inner .strict() 必需 (ADR-0006 #3)
    46	
    47	z.object({
    48	  modelUrl: z.string().min(1),
    49	  layers: z.array(layerSchema).default([]),
    50	  showWeights: z.boolean().default(false),
    51	}).strict();    // outer .strict() 同样必需
    52	```
    53	
    54	## tfjs consumer pattern
    55	
    56	E2 是 `@tensorflow/tfjs` 的第一个块级消费方。`createTfjsBridge` 把
    57	`tf.loadLayersModel` + `tf.LayersModel.dispose` 抽象为一个 `NnVizPhase`
    58	状态机，E3 后续 viz-block (React Flow + 模型推理) 复用相同骨架：
    59	
    60	- **Per-block isolated model**：每个 NodeView mount 调一次
    61	  `loadLayersModel(modelUrl)`；两个 nn-viz 块互不共享 weights / WebGL backend slot
    62	- **Loading state UI**：`loadLayersModel` 异步（model.json + 多 MB weight binaries），
    63	  bridge 暴露 `phase: 'loading'` 让 React 显示占位；不允许 silent 启动
    64	- **AbortSignal-driven cleanup**：NodeView unmount 触发 `controller.abort()` →
    65	  bridge 立即 `model.dispose()` 释放 WebGL 资源；mid-load 的 abort 同样 cleanup
    66	  （pending model 一旦 resolve 即 fire-and-forget dispose）
    67	- **Error-class triage at boundary**：bridge 在 catch 处按 message 模式分流到
    68	  `httpError` / `loadError` / `unknownError` 三种 phase。tfjs 不导出公开错误类
    69	  hierarchy，所以这里走字符串模式匹配；ADR-0006 #4 single authority — 上层 UI
    70	  不内联此分类规则，全部走 bridge consumer 端
    71	- **`tf.loadLayersModel` 是 runtime authority**：`tf` 由本包 import；本包不重
    72	  wrap loadLayersModel / 不内联 tfjs IOHandler（ADR-0006 #5 algorithm replication —
    73	  authority = `@tensorflow/tfjs`）。仅暴露 `LoadLayersModelFn` 注入点供测试
    74	
    75	## Invariants
    76	
    77	继承自 [block-foundation/CONTRACT.md](../block-foundation/CONTRACT.md#invariants)：
    78	`Defensive copy` / `Schema strictness` / `Default UI lookup` / `Serialize / parse hook ownership`。
    79	
    80	block-nn-viz 特定不变量：
    81	
    82	- **`coreName='nn-viz'` / `mdxComponent='NnViz'` / `kind='viz'`**: 字面值固定
    83	  ([RFC §1](../block-foundation/RFC.md#1-core-side)) ；kind=viz per
    84	  [ADR-0009](../../docs/decisions/ADR-0009-block-kind-union-expansion.md)（E1/E3 同 kind）
    85	- **Hook 命名 verb-as-prefix**: `serializeNnViz` / `parseNnViz` / `createTfjsBridge`
    86	  ([RFC §5](../block-foundation/RFC.md#5-serialize--parse-hook-ownership-scope-clarification))；
    87	  `uiId='default'` reserved (inherit foundation `Default UI lookup`)
    88	- **Nested .strict() (ADR-0006 #3)**：outer `propsSchema` 与 inner `layerSchema`
    89	  同时 `.strict()`。`core.test.ts` 含一条 "rejects unknown keys INSIDE a layer"
    90	  断言锁定 inner 层；移除任一处 `.strict()` 即破测试
    91	- **Headless 自给 (ADR-0003 D1)**: `core/` 仅依赖 `@skb/block-foundation` + `zod`；
    92	  React + tfjs + design-tokens 仅在 `ui-default/`
    93	- **propsSchema / serialize / parse single authority (ADR-0006 #4)**: 仅在
    94	  `core-definition.ts` 定义；serialize/parse 各调 `propsSchema.parse`
    95	  （boolean attrs 字符串 coerce → boolean，layers JSON-decode → array<LayerSpec>）
    96	- **Error 显式（不静默）**：load failure 走 `data-phase='httpError|loadError|unknownError'`；
    97	  nn-viz.css 把三者都 escalate 到 `--color-error` token

     1	import { nnVizCore } from './core-definition';
     2	import type { LayerSpec, NnVizMdastJsxElement, NnVizTiptapNode } from './serialize';
     3	
     4	/**
     5	 * MDX 解析 stub。Wave 3 mdx-bridge 在 mdastBlockToTiptap 看到
     6	 * mdxJsxFlowElement{name:'NnViz'} 时按 mdxComponent 路由到本函数（RFC §5）。
     7	 *
     8	 * Boolean attrs (`showWeights`) 三种 MDX 形式
     9	 * (mdast-util-mdx-jsx convention)：
    10	 *   - `<NnViz showWeights>` (boolean shorthand)   → attr.value === null  → true
    11	 *   - `<NnViz showWeights="true">`                → "true"  → true
    12	 *   - `<NnViz showWeights="false">`               → "false" → false
    13	 * 任何其他形式 throw — 不静默 false。
    14	 *
    15	 * `layers` 在 Wave 2 stub 中按 string-encoded JSON array 解析（serialize
    16	 * emits JSON.stringify）。Wave 3 mdx-bridge 接 expression-attr 后改为直接
    17	 * 接受 array literal 表达式；这层 stub 仅保证 round-trip 形状对齐。
    18	 *
    19	 * `modelUrl` 一律期望 string；null shorthand 仅 boolean attrs 适用。
    20	 */
    21	export function parseNnViz(node: NnVizMdastJsxElement): NnVizTiptapNode {
    22	  if (node.name !== nnVizCore.mdxComponent) {
    23	    throw new Error(
    24	      `parseNnViz: expected mdxComponent="${nnVizCore.mdxComponent}", got "${node.name}"`,
    25	    );
    26	  }
    27	  const rawProps: Record<string, string | boolean | LayerSpec[]> = {};
    28	  for (const attr of node.attributes) {
    29	    if (attr.name === 'showWeights') {
    30	      if (attr.value === null) {
    31	        rawProps[attr.name] = true;
    32	      } else if (attr.value === 'true' || attr.value === 'false') {
    33	        rawProps[attr.name] = attr.value === 'true';
    34	      } else {
    35	        throw new Error(
    36	          `parseNnViz: invalid showWeights attribute value: ${JSON.stringify(attr.value)}`,
    37	        );
    38	      }
    39	    } else if (attr.name === 'layers') {
    40	      if (attr.value === null) {
    41	        throw new Error(
    42	          'parseNnViz: attribute "layers" must have a string value (got null shorthand; only boolean attrs support shorthand)',
    43	        );
    44	      }
    45	      let parsed: unknown;
    46	      try {
    47	        parsed = JSON.parse(attr.value);
    48	      } catch {
    49	        throw new Error(
    50	          `parseNnViz: layers attribute is not valid JSON: ${JSON.stringify(attr.value)}`,
    51	        );
    52	      }
    53	      if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
    54	        throw new Error(
    55	          `parseNnViz: layers must decode to an array; got ${JSON.stringify(parsed)}`,
    56	        );
    57	      }
    58	      rawProps[attr.name] = parsed as LayerSpec[];
    59	    } else {
    60	      if (attr.value === null) {
    61	        throw new Error(
    62	          `parseNnViz: attribute "${attr.name}" must have a string value (got null shorthand; only boolean attrs support shorthand)`,
    63	        );
    64	      }
    65	      rawProps[attr.name] = attr.value;
    66	    }
    67	  }
    68	  const validated = nnVizCore.propsSchema.parse(rawProps);
    69	  return {
    70	    type: 'nn-viz',
    71	    attrs: {
    72	      modelUrl: validated.modelUrl,
    73	      layers: validated.layers,
    74	      showWeights: validated.showWeights,
    75	    },
    76	  };
    77	}

     1	import { nnVizCore } from './core-definition';
     2	
     3	/**
     4	 * MDX 序列化 stub。完整实现等 Wave 3 mdx-bridge routing table 落地（RFC §5）：
     5	 * mdx-bridge 拿到 TiptapNode{type:'nn-viz'} 时按 mdxComponent 字符串路由到本函数。
     6	 *
     7	 * Sister-pattern E1 (block-jupyter): boolean attrs string-form, structured
     8	 * data (libraries / layers) JSON-encoded for Wave 2; Wave 3 expression-attr
     9	 * upgrade emits raw arrays via mdx-bridge consumer.
    10	 */
    11	export interface LayerSpec {
    12	  readonly name: string;
    13	  readonly units: number;
    14	  readonly activation: 'relu' | 'softmax' | 'sigmoid' | 'tanh' | 'linear';
    15	}
    16	
    17	export interface NnVizTiptapNode {
    18	  readonly type: 'nn-viz';
    19	  readonly attrs: {
    20	    readonly modelUrl: string;
    21	    readonly layers: readonly LayerSpec[];
    22	    readonly showWeights: boolean;
    23	  };
    24	}
    25	
    26	/**
    27	 * `value` is `string | null` per mdast-util-mdx-jsx convention:
    28	 *   - `<NnViz showWeights>` (boolean shorthand)        → attribute with `value: null`
    29	 *   - `<NnViz showWeights="true">` / `"false"`         → string
    30	 *   - `<NnViz modelUrl="https://...">`                 → string (always)
    31	 *   - `<NnViz layers={[{...}]}>` (expression)          → handled in Wave 3 mdx-bridge
    32	 *     when expression-attr support lands; Wave 2 stub only emits string-form for
    33	 *     the array via JSON.stringify (mdx-bridge consumer will translate to expression).
    34	 *
    35	 * `parseNnViz` handles null shorthand for `showWeights`;
    36	 * `serializeNnViz` always emits string form for round-trip stability — null
    37	 * shorthand only on the parse side (mirror of block-math + block-jupyter pattern).
    38	 */
    39	export interface NnVizMdastJsxElement {
    40	  readonly type: 'mdxJsxFlowElement';
    41	  readonly name: string;
    42	  readonly attributes: ReadonlyArray<{
    43	    readonly type: 'mdxJsxAttribute';
    44	    readonly name: string;
    45	    readonly value: string | null;
    46	  }>;
    47	  readonly children: readonly unknown[];
    48	}
    49	
    50	export function serializeNnViz(node: NnVizTiptapNode): NnVizMdastJsxElement {
    51	  const validated = nnVizCore.propsSchema.parse(node.attrs);
    52	  return {
    53	    type: 'mdxJsxFlowElement',
    54	    name: nnVizCore.mdxComponent,
    55	    attributes: [
    56	      { type: 'mdxJsxAttribute', name: 'modelUrl', value: validated.modelUrl },
    57	      { type: 'mdxJsxAttribute', name: 'layers', value: JSON.stringify(validated.layers) },
    58	      { type: 'mdxJsxAttribute', name: 'showWeights', value: String(validated.showWeights) },
    59	    ],
    60	    children: [],
    61	  };
    62	}

     2	import type { BlockViewProps } from '@skb/block-foundation';
     3	import type { KernelAdapter, KernelEvent } from '@skb/kernel-adapter';
     4	import { PyodideAdapter } from '@skb/kernel-pyodide';
     5	import { jupyterCore } from '../core/core-definition';
     6	import { createKernelBridge, type KernelBridge, type KernelPhase } from './kernel-bridge';
     7	
     8	/**
     9	 * JupyterView — Tiptap NodeView for `kind='viz'` jupyter cell. Renders
    10	 *   - editable code textarea (line-numbered when `showLineNumbers`)
    11	 *   - status indicator driven by KernelPhase
    12	 *   - Run button (gated on phase ∈ {ready, finished, execError, kernelError})
    13	 *   - output panel: stdout/stderr stream + execute_result + display_data
    14	 *
    15	 * `optionalAdapter` lets tests inject a fake KernelAdapter; production code
    16	 * leaves it undefined and a per-mount PyodideAdapter is constructed (lazy
    17	 * — startSession is not called until either runOnLoad or user click).
    18	 *
    19	 * Mirrors MathView's "no explicit BlockUIDefinition<typeof ...> annotation"
    20	 * pattern (ADR-0003 inference rule; see math.ui.ts comment).
    21	 */
    22	
    23	interface OutputState {
    24	  readonly entries: ReadonlyArray<{
    25	    readonly id: number;
    26	    readonly stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr' | 'result' | 'display' | 'error';
    27	    readonly text: string;
    28	  }>;
    29	  readonly nextId: number;
    30	}
    31	
    32	const EMPTY_OUTPUT: OutputState = { entries: [], nextId: 0 };
    33	
    34	type OutputAction = { type: 'append'; event: KernelEvent } | { type: 'reset' };
    35	
    36	function outputReducer(state: OutputState, action: OutputAction): OutputState {
    37	  if (action.type === 'reset') return EMPTY_OUTPUT;
    38	  const event = action.event;
    39	  if (event.type === 'stdout' || event.type === 'stderr') {
    40	    return {
    41	      entries: [
    42	        ...state.entries,
    43	        { id: state.nextId, stream: event.type, text: event.text },
    44	      ],
    45	      nextId: state.nextId + 1,
    46	    };
    47	  }
    48	  if (event.type === 'execute_result' || event.type === 'display_data') {
    49	    const text = formatMime(event.data);
    50	    return {
    51	      entries: [
    52	        ...state.entries,
    53	        {
    54	          id: state.nextId,
    55	          stream: event.type === 'execute_result' ? 'result' : 'display',
    56	          text,
    57	        },
    58	      ],
    59	      nextId: state.nextId + 1,
    60	    };
    61	  }
    62	  if (event.type === 'error') {
    63	    const text = `${event.ename}: ${event.evalue}\n${event.traceback.join('\n')}`;
    64	    return {
    65	      entries: [
    66	        ...state.entries,
    67	        { id: state.nextId, stream: 'error', text },
    68	      ],
    69	      nextId: state.nextId + 1,
    70	    };
    71	  }
    72	  return state;
    73	}
    74	
    75	function formatMime(data: Record<string, unknown>): string {
    76	  const text = data['text/plain'];
    77	  if (typeof text === 'string') return text;
    78	  return JSON.stringify(data);
    79	}

    81	export interface JupyterViewProps
    82	  extends BlockViewProps<typeof jupyterCore.propsSchema> {
    83	  /** Override the adapter (test injection). */
    84	  readonly adapter?: KernelAdapter;
    85	}
    86	
    87	export function JupyterView({ props, adapter }: JupyterViewProps): JSX.Element {
    88	  const [phase, setPhase] = useReducer(
    89	    (_prev: KernelPhase, next: KernelPhase) => next,
    90	    { type: 'idle' } as KernelPhase,
    91	  );
    92	  const [output, dispatchOutput] = useReducer(outputReducer, EMPTY_OUTPUT);
    93	  const bridgeRef = useRef<KernelBridge | null>(null);
    94	  const codeRef = useRef(props.code);
    95	  codeRef.current = props.code;
    96	
    97	  const adapterRef = useRef<KernelAdapter | null>(null);
    98	  if (adapterRef.current === null) {
    99	    adapterRef.current = adapter ?? new PyodideAdapter({ boot: { libraries: props.libraries } });
   100	  }
   101	  const liveAdapter = adapterRef.current;
   102	  const runOnLoadAtMount = useRef(props.runOnLoad);
   103	
   104	  useEffect(() => {
   105	    const controller = new AbortController();
   106	    const bridge = createKernelBridge({
   107	      adapter: liveAdapter,
   108	      sessionId: `jupyter-${cryptoRandomId()}`,
   109	      signal: controller.signal,
   110	      onPhase: setPhase,
   111	      onEvent: (event) => dispatchOutput({ type: 'append', event }),
   112	    });
   113	    bridgeRef.current = bridge;
   114	    if (runOnLoadAtMount.current) {
   115	      void bridge.run(codeRef.current);
   116	    }
   117	    return () => {
   118	      controller.abort();
   119	      bridgeRef.current = null;
   120	    };
   121	  }, [liveAdapter]);
   122	
   123	  const onRun = useCallback(() => {
   124	    dispatchOutput({ type: 'reset' });
   125	    void bridgeRef.current?.run(props.code);
   126	  }, [props.code]);
   127	
   128	  const lines = useMemo(() => splitLines(props.code), [props.code]);
   129	
   130	  const runDisabled =
   131	    phase.type === 'starting' || phase.type === 'running';
   132	  const statusLabel = describePhase(phase);
   133	
   134	  return (
   135	    <div data-block="jupyter" data-phase={phase.type}>
   136	      <div className="skb-jupyter-toolbar">
   137	        <button
   138	          type="button"
   139	          className="skb-jupyter-run"
   140	          onClick={onRun}
   141	          disabled={runDisabled}
   142	          aria-label="Run cell"
   143	        >
   144	          {phase.type === 'running' ? 'Running…' : 'Run'}
   145	        </button>
   146	        <span className="skb-jupyter-status" role="status">
   147	          {statusLabel}
   148	        </span>
   149	      </div>
   150	      <pre
   151	        className="skb-jupyter-code"
   152	        data-line-numbers={props.showLineNumbers ? 'true' : 'false'}
   153	      >
   154	        {props.showLineNumbers ? (
   155	          lines.map((line, i) => (
   156	            <span key={i} className="skb-jupyter-line">
   157	              <span className="skb-jupyter-lineno" aria-hidden="true">
   158	                {i + 1}
   159	              </span>
   160	              <code>{line}</code>
   161	            </span>
   162	          ))
   163	        ) : (
   164	          <code>{props.code}</code>
   165	        )}
   166	      </pre>
   167	      {output.entries.length > 0 && (
   168	        <div className="skb-jupyter-output" aria-live="polite">
   169	          {output.entries.map((entry) => (
   170	            <pre key={entry.id} data-stream={entry.stream}>
   171	              {entry.text}
   172	            </pre>
   173	          ))}
   174	        </div>
   175	      )}
   176	    </div>
   177	  );
   178	}
   179	
   180	function describePhase(phase: KernelPhase): string {
   181	  switch (phase.type) {
   182	    case 'idle':
   183	      return 'Idle';
   184	    case 'starting':
   185	      return 'Loading kernel…';
   186	    case 'ready':
   187	      return 'Ready';
   188	    case 'running':
   189	      return 'Running';
   190	    case 'finished':
   191	      return 'Finished';
   192	    case 'execError':
   193	      return `Error: ${phase.ename}`;
   194	    case 'kernelError':
   195	      return `Kernel error: ${phase.message}`;
   196	  }
   197	}
   198	
   199	function splitLines(code: string): string[] {
   200	  if (code === '') return [''];
   201	  return code.split('\n');
   202	}
   203	
   204	function cryptoRandomId(): string {
   205	  if (
   206	    typeof globalThis.crypto !== 'undefined' &&
   207	    typeof globalThis.crypto.randomUUID === 'function'
   208	  ) {
   209	    return globalThis.crypto.randomUUID();
   210	  }
   211	  return Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
   212	}

     4	/**
     5	 * Byte-equality corpus for renderMath authority (ADR-0006 item #5).
     6	 *
     7	 * `renderMath` is the single import point for KaTeX in this package; both
     8	 * Math.tsx (React/NodeView path) and Math.astro (SSR path) call it. This
     9	 * suite exercises a representative input corpus to:
    10	 *   1. catch silent regressions if a future edit re-inlines `katex.renderToString`
    11	 *      with diverging options (drift detector for the algorithm-replication audit);
    12	 *   2. assert error-explicit behavior — invalid LaTeX must surface as
    13	 *      `.katex-error` in the output (spec D1 "red error box with the source
    14	 *      visible"; not silent fallback).
    15	 *
    16	 * KaTeX is the runtime authority — these tests do NOT pin the exact HTML byte
    17	 * shape (KaTeX patch versions can shift markup); they assert structural
    18	 * invariants (root class, displayMode discriminator, error-class presence)
    19	 * that any in-package option-divergence would break.
    20	 */
    21	describe('renderMath (KaTeX SSR authority)', () => {
    22	  it('renders inline expression with displayMode=false (no display block)', () => {
    23	    const html = renderMath('a^2 + b^2', false);
    24	    expect(html).toMatch(/class="katex"/);
    25	    expect(html).not.toMatch(/class="katex-display"/);
    26	  });
    27	
    28	  it('renders display expression with displayMode=true (wraps in katex-display)', () => {
    29	    const html = renderMath('\\sum_{i=0}^n x_i', true);
    30	    expect(html).toMatch(/class="katex-display"/);
    31	    expect(html).toMatch(/class="katex"/);
    32	  });
    33	
    34	  it('renders multiline displayed expression (multi-row aligned env)', () => {
    35	    const html = renderMath(
    36	      '\\begin{aligned} a &= 1 \\\\ b &= 2 \\end{aligned}',
    37	      true,
    38	    );
    39	    expect(html).toMatch(/class="katex-display"/);
    40	    // multi-line rendering produces multiple mord/mrel spans
    41	    expect(html).toMatch(/class="katex"/);
    42	    expect(html.length).toBeGreaterThan(100);
    43	  });
    44	
    45	  it('renders malformed LaTeX with errorColor inline + source visible (throwOnError=false invariant)', () => {
    46	    const html = renderMath('\\notARealCommand{x}', false);
    47	    // KaTeX with throwOnError=false renders unknown commands inline with
    48	    // errorColor (default #cc0000); source string is preserved verbatim so the
    49	    // user can see the offending expression (spec D1 "red error box with the
    50	    // source visible"). math.css uses [data-block='math'] [style*="cc0000"]
    51	    // upgrade selector to bind --color-error token + bordered box.
    52	    expect(html).toMatch(/class="katex"/);

    55	  });
    56

     4	/**

     6	 *
     7	 * `renderPdf` is the single import point for iframe URL + data-attr
     8	 * construction in this package; both Pdf.tsx (React/NodeView path) and

    10	 * corpus to:

    12	 *      (drift detector for the algorithm-replication audit);
    13	 *   2. assert PDF Open Parameters fragment shape (`#page=N`) — required for
    14	 *      browser-native PDF viewer to honor initial page;
    15	 *   3. cover the missing-file fallback path: even with a bogus `src`, the
    16	 *      descriptor is structurally valid so the wrapper container + iframe
    17	 *      shell render and the browser's native viewer surfaces its own
    18	 *      empty-state UI.
    19	 *
    20	 * Browser-native PDF viewer is the runtime authority — these tests do NOT
    21	 * pin the exact rendered PDF visuals (browsers diverge); they assert
    22	 * structural invariants (iframeSrc fragment, data-attr shape, identity of
    23	 * src round-trip).
    24	 */
    25	describe('renderPdf (iframe SSR authority)', () => {
    26	  it('produces iframeSrc with #page=N fragment for default page=1', () => {
    27	    const desc = renderPdf('/files/paper.pdf', 1, false);
    28	    expect(desc.iframeSrc).toBe('/files/paper.pdf#page=1');
    29	    expect(desc.dataAttrs['data-block']).toBe('pdf');
    30	    expect(desc.dataAttrs['data-page']).toBe('1');
    31	    expect(desc.dataAttrs['data-searchable']).toBe('false');
    32	  });
    33	
    34	  it('produces iframeSrc with #page=N for arbitrary page', () => {
    35	    const desc = renderPdf('https://example.com/doc.pdf', 42, true);
    36	    expect(desc.iframeSrc).toBe('https://example.com/doc.pdf#page=42');
    37	    expect(desc.dataAttrs['data-page']).toBe('42');
    38	    expect(desc.dataAttrs['data-searchable']).toBe('true');
    39	  });
    40	
    41	  it('preserves src verbatim (no encoding / normalization in render layer)', () => {
    42	    // src normalization is propsSchema's job; renderPdf is downstream and must
    43	    // not double-normalize. Test pinning string identity.
    44	    const desc = renderPdf('/files/My Doc.pdf', 1, false);
    45	    expect(desc.src).toBe('/files/My Doc.pdf');
    46	    expect(desc.iframeSrc).toBe('/files/My Doc.pdf#page=1');
    47	  });
    48	
    49	  it('handles missing-file-style src (browser viewer surfaces its own empty state)', () => {
    50	    // Even with bogus src, the descriptor is structurally valid — Pdf.tsx /
    51	    // Pdf.astro both render an iframe shell + container; the browser's native
    52	    // PDF viewer renders its own empty-doc UI on the inside. Wave 2 invariant:
    53	    // never silent-fallback to alt text; always show the iframe shell so users

    55	    const desc = renderPdf('/does-not-exist.pdf', 1, false);

    59

    62	    const b = renderPdf('/files/paper.pdf', 5, false);
    63	    expect(a.iframeSrc).not.toBe(b.iframeSrc);
    64	    expect(a.dataAttrs['data-page']).toBe('1');
    65	    expect(b.dataAttrs['data-page']).toBe('5');
    66	  });
    67	
    68	  it('strips pre-existing fragment from src before appending #page= (R2-1 hazard)', () => {
    69	    // `src` may carry an external fragment (e.g. anchor in a publishing CMS:
    70	    // "doc.pdf#section=intro"). PDF Open Parameters URLs are not mergeable —
    71	    // only one `#…` segment per URL, and `page=N` must be authoritative for
    72	    // the chosen page. Anything else would yield `doc.pdf#section=intro#page=3`
    73	    // which the browser parses as fragment="section=intro#page=3" and ignores
    74	    // the page= directive entirely.
    75	    const desc = renderPdf('doc.pdf#section=intro', 3, false);
    76	    expect(desc.iframeSrc).toBe('doc.pdf#page=3');
    77	    expect(desc.src).toBe('doc.pdf#section=intro'); // src verbatim per contract
    78	  });
    79	
    80	  it('handles src with empty fragment ("foo.pdf#") cleanly', () => {
    81	    const desc = renderPdf('foo.pdf#', 1, false);
    82	    expect(desc.iframeSrc).toBe('foo.pdf#page=1');
    83	  });

     1	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
     2	import { resolve } from 'node:path';
     3	import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
     4	import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
     5	import { PdfRenderView } from '../ui-default/Pdf';
     6	import { renderPdf } from '../ui-default/render-pdf';
     7	
     8	/**
     9	 * Byte-equivalence regression for ADR-0006 #5 (algorithm replication single
    10	 * source). Pdf.tsx (React/NodeView path) and Pdf.astro (SSR path) MUST both
    11	 * call `renderPdf(...)` and emit identical container + iframe markup.
    12	 *
    13	 * Two-tier verification strategy (Astro `.astro` files cannot be invoked
    14	 * inside vitest without running the Astro compiler, so we mix runtime + AST
    15	 * checks):
    16	 *
    17	 * 1. **Runtime SSR** of `PdfRenderView` via `react-dom/server.renderToStaticMarkup`.
    18	 *    Asserts the React path renders exactly the descriptor produced by
    19	 *    `renderPdf` — `data-block` / `data-page` / `data-searchable` attributes
    20	 *    on the wrapper div + `<iframe src=… loading="lazy" title>`.
    21	 * 2. **Static analysis** of `Pdf.astro` source: must `import { renderPdf } from
    22	 *    './render-pdf'`, must invoke `renderPdf(`, must emit a `<div>` wrapper
    23	 *    with the same three `desc.dataAttrs[…]` bindings, must emit an iframe
    24	 *    using `desc.iframeSrc` + `loading="lazy"`. This is the structural
    25	 *    equivalence guarantee the codex 5.5 R2-3 review asked for: even though we
    26	 *    cannot literally byte-compare two HTML strings, drift in either file is
    27	 *    detectable — runtime regression catches Pdf.tsx changes, AST regex
    28	 *    catches Pdf.astro changes, and the shared `renderPdf` authority + its
    29	 *    own ssr-render.test.ts corpus guarantees the underlying values match.
    30	 *
    31	 * What this does NOT verify (Wave 2 documented gap):
    32	 *   - The compiled Astro output is byte-equal to the React SSR output. Astro
    33	 *     adds its own scoped-style attributes, hydration directives, etc.; that
    34	 *     comparison would require a full Astro toolchain in vitest. Wave 3
    35	 *     mdx-doctor PR will run a `mdx-bridge` round-trip fixture for `<Pdf>` that
    36	 *     exercises this end-to-end via the apps/site build, closing the gap from
    37	 *     the consumer side.
    38	 */
    39	
    40	// __dirname-style path resolution. Vitest runs with cwd=packages/block-pdf/,
    41	// so we anchor source paths relative to that. Avoids `import.meta.url` quirks
    42	// under happy-dom (fileURLToPath rejects non-file: URLs in some test runners).
    43	const PDF_ASTRO_PATH = resolve('src/ui-default/Pdf.astro');
    44	const PDF_TSX_PATH = resolve('src/ui-default/Pdf.tsx');
    45	
    46	describe('Pdf.tsx + Pdf.astro byte-equivalence (ADR-0006 #5)', () => {
    47	  it('PdfRenderView SSR markup matches renderPdf descriptor verbatim', () => {
    48	    const props = { src: '/files/paper.pdf', page: 7, searchable: true };
    49	    const desc = renderPdf(props.src, props.page, props.searchable);
    50	    const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<PdfRenderView props={props} />);
    51	
    52	    expect(html).toContain(`data-block="${desc.dataAttrs['data-block']}"`);
    53	    expect(html).toContain(`data-page="${desc.dataAttrs['data-page']}"`);
    54	    expect(html).toContain(
    55	      `data-searchable="${desc.dataAttrs['data-searchable']}"`,
    56	    );
    57	    expect(html).toContain(`src="${desc.iframeSrc}"`);
    58	    expect(html).toContain('loading="lazy"');
    59	    expect(html).toContain(`title="PDF: ${desc.src}"`);
    60	  });
    61	
    62	  it('PdfRenderView strips fragment from src in iframeSrc (R2-1 regression)', () => {
    63	    const props = { src: 'doc.pdf#section=intro', page: 4, searchable: false };
    64	    const html = renderToStaticMarkup(<PdfRenderView props={props} />);
    65	    expect(html).toContain('src="doc.pdf#page=4"');
    66	    expect(html).not.toContain('section=intro#page=');
    67	  });
    68	
    69	  it('Pdf.astro source imports renderPdf authority + uses descriptor bindings', () => {
    70	    const astroSource = readFileSync(PDF_ASTRO_PATH, 'utf8');
    71	
    72	    // Authority import is mandatory — no inline iframe URL construction.
    73	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(/import\s+\{\s*renderPdf\s*\}\s+from\s+['"]\.\/render-pdf['"]/);
    74	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(/renderPdf\s*\(/);
    75	
    76	    // Wrapper container + three data-attr bindings (sister-doc to Pdf.tsx).
    77	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(/data-block=\{?desc\.dataAttrs\['data-block'\]/);
    78	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(/data-page=\{?desc\.dataAttrs\['data-page'\]/);
    79	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(
    80	      /data-searchable=\{?desc\.dataAttrs\['data-searchable'\]/,
    81	    );
    82	
    83	    // iframe uses the descriptor's iframeSrc (not raw src) + lazy loading.
    84	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(/src=\{?desc\.iframeSrc\}?/);
    85	    expect(astroSource).toMatch(/loading=['"]lazy['"]/);
    86	
    87	    // Drift sentinel — the file must NOT have an inline `${src}#page=` template
    88	    // literal that would bypass renderPdf authority.
    89	    expect(astroSource).not.toMatch(/\$\{src\}#page=/);
    90	    expect(astroSource).not.toMatch(/`\$\{[^}]+\}#page=/);
    91	  });
    92	
    93	  it('Pdf.tsx source imports renderPdf authority + uses descriptor bindings (sister sentinel)', () => {
    94	    // Symmetric drift sentinel for the React side. ssr-render.test.ts already
    95	    // exercises renderPdf directly; this one specifically locks down the
    96	    // Pdf.tsx call site.
    97	    const tsxSource = readFileSync(PDF_TSX_PATH, 'utf8');
    98	
    99	    expect(tsxSource).toMatch(/import\s+\{\s*renderPdf\s*\}\s+from\s+['"]\.\/render-pdf['"]/);
   100	    expect(tsxSource).toMatch(/renderPdf\s*\(/);
   101	    expect(tsxSource).not.toMatch(/\$\{[^}]+\}#page=/);
   102	  });
   103	});

    17	
    18	interface FlowNode {
    19	  id: string;
    20	  label: string;
    21	  type: 'agent' | 'tool' | 'memory' | 'router';
    22	  position: { x: number; y: number };
    23	}
    24	
    25	interface FlowEdge {
    26	  id: string;
    27	  source: string;
    28	  target: string;
    29	  label?: string;
    30	}

    33	  nodes: FlowNode[];
    34	  edges: FlowEdge[];
    35	}

    38	
    39	const NODE_W = 140;
    40	const NODE_H = 40;
    41	const PAD = 20;
    42	
    43	const nodeMap = new Map(nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
    44	
    45	const minX = nodes.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.min(...nodes.map((n) => n.position.x));
    46	const minY = nodes.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.min(...nodes.map((n) => n.position.y));
    47	const maxX = nodes.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.max(...nodes.map((n) => n.position.x));
    48	const maxY = nodes.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.max(...nodes.map((n) => n.position.y));
    49	
    50	const width = Math.max(maxX - minX + NODE_W + PAD * 2, NODE_W + PAD * 2);
    51	const height = Math.max(maxY - minY + NODE_H + PAD * 2, NODE_H + PAD * 2);
    52	
    53	const offX = PAD - minX;
    54	const offY = PAD - minY;
    55	---

    69	      if (!s || !t) return null;

     9	 * Design lessons codified here (same shape as E1):
    10	 *
    11	 * 1. **Per-block isolation**: every mount creates its own model — two
    12	 *    nn-viz blocks on the same page do NOT share weights / layer state.
    13	 *    `tf.LayersModel` instances are independent disposables.
    14	 * 2. **Loading state mandatory**: `loadLayersModel` is async (model files
    15	 *    are typically multi-MB downloads). Bridge surfaces `phase: 'loading'`
    16	 *    so the React layer renders a placeholder rather than empty SVG.
    17	 * 3. **AbortSignal-driven cleanup**: NodeView unmount aborts; the bridge
    18	 *    discards the in-flight load, and any model that resolves AFTER abort
    19	 *    gets `dispose()`'d immediately to free WebGL backends. No silent leak.
    20	 * 4. **Error-class triage**: distinct phases for HTTP fetch failure (`httpError`),
    21	 *    tfjs internal load failure (`loadError`), and other unexpected throws
    22	 *    (`unknownError`). UI does NOT need to import tfjs-internal error classes;
    23	 *    the discriminant kind is derived at the bridge boundary.
    24	 *
    25	 * Framework-agnostic — no React imports — so the bridge can be unit-tested
    26	 * without happy-dom and reused from non-React surfaces (e.g. Wave 3 training
    27	 * dashboards).
    28	 */
    29	
    30	export type NnVizPhase =
    31	  /** before load() is called */
    32	  | { type: 'idle' }
    33	  /** loadLayersModel in flight */
    34	  | { type: 'loading' }
    35	  /** model live and ready to inspect */
    36	  | { type: 'ready'; model: LayersModel }
    37	  /** fetch failed (network / 404) */
    38	  | { type: 'httpError'; message: string }
    39	  /** tfjs load / parse failed (corrupt model.json, unsupported layer, etc.) */
    40	  | { type: 'loadError'; message: string }
    41	  /** anything else thrown during load */
    42	  | { type: 'unknownError'; message: string };
    43	
    44	export type LoadLayersModelFn = (modelUrl: string) => Promise<LayersModel>;
    45	
    46	export interface TfjsBridgeOptions {
    47	  readonly modelUrl: string;
    48	  /**
    49	   * Aborts pending load + disposes any model that resolves after abort.
    50	   * NodeView passes its unmount signal here.
    51	   */
    52	  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
    53	  /**
    54	   * Notified when phase changes. The React adapter wraps this with `useState`
    55	   * (see `NnViz.tsx`); non-React consumers can patch their own store.
    56	   */
    57	  readonly onPhase: (phase: NnVizPhase) => void;
    58	  /**
    59	   * tfjs `loadLayersModel` injection point. Production code passes
    60	   * `tf.loadLayersModel`; tests pass mocks. Lets us cover load lifecycle
    61	   * + error branches without booting a real WebGL backend.
    62	   */
    63	  readonly loadLayersModel: LoadLayersModelFn;
    64	}
    65	
    66	export interface TfjsBridge {
    67	  /**
    68	   * Boot model load. Idempotent: a second call after `phase==='ready'`
    69	   * returns the same model; mid-load second calls await the first.
    70	   * Errors land via `onPhase` with one of the *Error variants; the
    71	   * returned promise resolves once load has completed OR errored.
    72	   */
    73	  load(): Promise<void>;
    74	}
    75	
    76	/**
    77	 * HTTP-style errors thrown by tfjs IOHandlers carry status codes in the
    78	 * message — match patterns rather than `instanceof` since tfjs does not
    79	 * export a public error class hierarchy.
    80	 */
    81	function classifyLoadError(err: unknown): NnVizPhase {
    82	  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
    83	  if (
    84	    /\b(404|403|500|502|503|504)\b/.test(message) ||
    85	    /HTTP|fetch|network|Failed to fetch/i.test(message)
    86	  ) {
    87	    return { type: 'httpError', message };
    88	  }
    89	  if (
    90	    /JSON|parse|model\.json|unsupported|topology|invalid/i.test(message) ||
    91	    /tensorflow|tfjs/i.test(message)
    92	  ) {
    93	    return { type: 'loadError', message };
    94	  }
    95	  return { type: 'unknownError', message };
    96	}
    97	
    98	export function createTfjsBridge(options: TfjsBridgeOptions): TfjsBridge {
    99	  const { modelUrl, signal, onPhase, loadLayersModel } = options;
   100	  let model: LayersModel | null = null;
   101	  let loadPromise: Promise<void> | null = null;
   102	  let disposed = false;
   103	
   104	  const dispose = (): void => {
   105	    if (disposed) return;
   106	    disposed = true;
   107	    if (model !== null) {
   108	      const m = model;
   109	      model = null;
   110	      try {
   111	        m.dispose();
   112	      } catch {
   113	        // ignore double-dispose / backend errors
   114	      }
   115	    }
   116	  };
   117	
   118	  signal.addEventListener('abort', dispose, { once: true });
   119	
   120	  const load = async (): Promise<void> => {
   121	    if (disposed) return;
   122	    if (model !== null) return;
   123	    if (loadPromise !== null) return loadPromise;
   124	    onPhase({ type: 'loading' });
   125	    loadPromise = (async () => {
   126	      try {
   127	        const m = await loadLayersModel(modelUrl);
   128	        if (disposed) {
   129	          try {
   130	            m.dispose();
   131	          } catch {
   132	            // ignore
   133	          }
   134	          return;
   135	        }
   136	        model = m;
   137	        onPhase({ type: 'ready', model: m });
   138	      } catch (cause) {
   139	        if (disposed) return;
   140	        onPhase(classifyLoadError(cause));
   141	      }
   142	    })();
   143	    return loadPromise;
   144	  };
   145	
   146	  return { load };
   147	}
